column2: On the authority of al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), from the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), who said: “Righteousness is good character, and sin is what wavers in your soul and you dislike people coming to know of it.” Reported by Muslim.
And on the authority of Wābiṣah ibn Maʿbad (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) and he said:

“You have come to ask about righteousness?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Consult your heart. Righteousness is that with which the soul is at peace and the heart is at peace, and sin is what wavers in the soul and goes back and forth in the breast, even if people give you a ruling and give you rulings again.” A ḥasan hadith;
we have narrated it in the Musnads of the two imams Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and al-Dārimī with an authentic chain.
Al-birr (“righteousness”): its main part; it denotes what the Sharīʿah requires, whether as an obligation or a recommendation.

Ḥusn al-khuluq (“good character”): fairness in dealings, gentleness in argument, justice in judgements, giving and kindness in times of ease, putting others first in times of hardship, and other praiseworthy qualities.
Wa-l-ithm (“and sin”): the wrongdoing.
“What wavers in your breast”: what stirs in the soul and goes back and forth in the heart, with which it is not at peace.
“And you dislike”: with a religious dislike,
“people coming to know of it”: their notable and best people, before whom one feels shame.
“With which the soul is at peace”: in which the good soul finds rest.
“People give you a ruling”: their scholars, as in the narration, “even if the muftīs give you a ruling”,
“and give you rulings again”: to the contrary, because they speak only according to the outward aspect of matters, not their inner reality.
The lemma is printed حالك في صدرك, evidently for حاك في صدرك (“what wavers in your breast”).
A criterion for righteousness and sin.
Encouragement to good character.
Truth and falsehood are not confused for the discerning believer; rather, he recognises the truth by the light in his heart, and recoils from falsehood and rejects it.

A great miracle of the Prophet ﷺ, in that he told Wābiṣah what was in his mind before he spoke of it, and put it in the form of a question seeking confirmation, to make his knowledge and full awareness of it all the more evident.
A ruling does not remove the doubt if the one seeking it is someone whose breast Allah has opened,

and the muftī gave the ruling merely on conjecture or inclination to whim, without evidence from the Sharīʿah. But where what the ruling permits is supported by evidence from the Sharīʿah, the one seeking it must accept it, even if his heart is not at ease with it,
such as breaking the fast when travelling or ill, shortening the prayer when travelling, and the like, with which the hearts of many ignorant people are not at ease.
The printed text reads كالمطر في السفر, evidently for كالفطر في السفر (“breaking the fast when travelling”).
